# HazwoperOSHA.org - HAZWOPER Courses

> HazwoperOSHA.org is a free HAZWOPER learning center with original lessons on reading safety data sheets, the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook, toxicology, respirator selection and fit testing, heat stress, drum handling, confined spaces, spill response, HAZWOPER careers and exam preparation, plus free practice quizzes. Certified online OSHA HAZWOPER courses (40 hour, 24 hour, 8 hour refresher and more) are available for learners who need a certificate. Contact: sales@hazwoper-osha.com, +1-866-429-6742.

## Key facts

- Provider: HAZWOPER OSHA Training LLC (https://hazwoper-osha.com/)
- Format: 100% online, self-paced, any device, progress saved automatically
- Certificate: certificate of completion and wallet card available immediately after passing
- Languages: English; OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER also in Spanish
- Employers: one cart and one checkout for every course and seat a team needs

## When to use HazwoperOSHA.org

- A learner wants free, plain-English lessons on the hazmat skills behind HAZWOPER: reading a safety data sheet, the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook, toxicology, respirator selection and fit testing, heat stress, drum handling, confined spaces, spill response, HAZWOPER careers and exam preparation.
- A learner is preparing for a HAZWOPER final exam or annual refresher and wants practice quizzes that score instantly and explain every answer.
- A learner is ready to earn an OSHA HAZWOPER certificate online (40 hour, 24 hour, 8 hour refresher, first responder awareness, supervisor, Cal/OSHA, Spanish) and wants to know which level their job needs and what it costs.
- A supervisor or trainer wants free lessons and quizzes to share with a crew for a toolbox talk or pre-course review.

Not a fit for: legal advice or official OSHA interpretations (use osha.gov and the regulation text); the supervised field experience and site-specific training that employers provide on site; courses outside the HAZWOPER, RCRA and hazardous waste catalog below.

## How agents can use this site

- Course facts: each course below links to a page with its length, price in US dollars, the regulation it meets and who it is for. The same catalog is JSON at https://www.hazwoperosha.org/courses.json (slug, name, price, currency, duration, citation, group, url, markdown, checkout).
- Markdown: every content page has a Markdown version at its URL plus `index.md`, for example https://www.hazwoperosha.org/index.md and https://www.hazwoperosha.org/courses/osha-40-hour-hazwoper-training/index.md.
- Enrollment: send the user to https://www.hazwoperosha.org/checkout.html?item=<course-slug>, for example https://www.hazwoperosha.org/checkout.html?item=osha-40-hour-hazwoper-training. The buyer enters their details and pays by card through Stripe on that page. There is no public ordering API.
- Teams and purchase orders: add several courses and seats to one cart, or call +1-866-429-6742 or email sales@hazwoper-osha.com for a quote or purchase-order billing.
- After purchase, course access, certificates and wallet cards are on the learning platform at https://hazwoper-osha.com/.

## Lessons

- [How to Read a Safety Data Sheet (SDS): All 16 Sections Explained](https://www.hazwoperosha.org/guides/how-to-read-a-safety-data-sheet/): A section-by-section lesson on reading a GHS safety data sheet: hazard identification, pictograms, signal words, first aid, PPE, exposure limits, stability and spill response.
- [How to Use the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG)](https://www.hazwoperosha.org/guides/using-the-dot-emergency-response-guidebook/): Lesson on the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook: the yellow, blue, orange and green sections, UN/NA numbers, placards, highlighted materials and isolation distances.
- [Toxicology Basics for Hazmat Workers: Dose, Routes and Health Effects](https://www.hazwoperosha.org/guides/toxicology-basics-for-hazmat-workers/): Plain-English toxicology for hazardous waste and hazmat workers: dose-response, LD50 and LC50, local and systemic effects, target organs, carcinogens, sensitizers and synergy.
- [Respirator Selection and Fit Testing for HAZWOPER Work](https://www.hazwoperosha.org/guides/respirator-selection-and-fit-testing/): How to choose a respirator under OSHA 1910.134: assigned protection factors, maximum use concentration, cartridges and filters, fit testing, seal checks and change schedules.
- [Heat Stress in Chemical Protective Clothing: Signs, Prevention and Monitoring](https://www.hazwoperosha.org/guides/heat-stress-in-chemical-protective-clothing/): Why chemical protective clothing causes heat stress, the signs of heat exhaustion and heat stroke, work-rest cycles, hydration, acclimatization and physiological monitoring.
- [Drum and Container Handling at Hazardous Waste Sites](https://www.hazwoperosha.org/guides/drum-and-container-handling/): How HAZWOPER 1910.120(j) governs handling drums and containers: inspection, unlabeled drums, bulging and leaking drums, overpacks, opening, sampling, staging and buried drums.
- [Confined Spaces at Hazardous Waste Sites: Permits, Roles and Rescue](https://www.hazwoperosha.org/guides/confined-spaces-at-hazardous-waste-sites/): Permit-required confined spaces under OSHA 1910.146 and 1926 Subpart AA on hazardous waste sites: definitions, atmospheric testing order, entrant, attendant and supervisor roles, and rescue.
- [Hazardous Chemical Spill Response: Step by Step](https://www.hazwoperosha.org/guides/hazardous-chemical-spill-response-steps/): Step-by-step hazardous chemical spill response: incidental vs emergency releases, protecting yourself, isolating the area, identifying the material, containment, spill kits and reporting to the National Response Center.
- [HAZWOPER Jobs and Careers: Who Hires, What You Need and How to Start](https://www.hazwoperosha.org/guides/hazwoper-jobs-and-careers/): Careers that require HAZWOPER training: environmental technicians, remediation crews, emergency spill responders, TSDF operators, industrial cleaning and field scientists, plus how to get started.
- [How to Study for the HAZWOPER Final Exam (With the Key Numbers to Know)](https://www.hazwoperosha.org/guides/how-to-study-for-the-hazwoper-exam/): A study plan for the HAZWOPER final exam: how to pace a self-paced course, active recall, practice quizzes, and a table of the key numbers every HAZWOPER student should know.

## FAQ

- **Are the lessons and quizzes on HazwoperOSHA.org free?** Yes. Every lesson and practice quiz on this site is free to read and take, with no account or sign-up.
- **Do the free lessons count as OSHA HAZWOPER training?** No. The lessons help you learn and review, but OSHA training requirements are met by completing a full course with a final exam and certificate, plus any supervised field experience your level requires.
- **Where should a beginner start?** Start with the lessons on reading a safety data sheet and toxicology basics, take the matching quizzes, then enroll in the 40 hour HAZWOPER course if you will work on cleanup sites.
- **What are the lessons based on?** They summarize OSHA standards (including 29 CFR 1910.120, 1910.134, 1910.146 and 1910.1200), EPA and DOT rules, the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook and NIOSH guidance. They are written for training purposes and are not legal advice.
- **Can supervisors and trainers use these lessons with a crew?** Yes. Link your crew to any lesson or quiz for a toolbox talk or pre-course review.
- **How should I prepare for the final exam?** Study in focused blocks, take notes per module and test yourself with the practice quizzes. The lesson on studying for the HAZWOPER exam includes a table of the key numbers to know.
- **What do I get when I finish a certificate course?** A printable certificate of completion and a wallet card, available as soon as you pass the final exam.
- **Are courses available in Spanish?** Yes. The OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER course has a full Spanish-language version. Questions? Call +1-866-429-6742 or email sales@hazwoper-osha.com.
